name: Cable Triceps Pushdown
summary: An upper-arm isolation exercise that targets the triceps brachii by extending the elbows against cable resistance from a high pulley.

setup: Attach a straight or angled bar to a high cable pulley.
Grasp the attachment with an overhand grip, roughly shoulder-width or slightly narrower.
Step back slightly, hinge forward slightly at the hips, and pin your upper arms against the sides of your torso.
steps: Drive the attachment downward by contracting your triceps until your elbows are fully extended.
Pause briefly at the bottom to accentuate the peak contraction.
Control the attachment back upward by flexing the elbows until your forearms are roughly parallel to the floor or slightly above, keeping your elbows fixed in place.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you push the bar down into full extension; inhale as you control the return upward.
cues: Keep elbows glued to your ribs

common_faults.fault: Flaring the elbows outward or allowing them to drift forward during the eccentric phase.
common_faults.correction: Keep your upper arms pinned to your torso so the movement isolates the elbow joint exclusively.

common_faults.fault: Using torso momentum or leaning heavily over the bar to press the weight down.
common_faults.correction: Maintain a steady torso angle with an engaged core and select a manageable load that does not require body swing.

precautions: Avoid aggressively hyperextending or snapping the elbow joint at the bottom of the movement.
